feature1.prompt: When running pytest with the --pdb option, tests that are individually marked as skipped should bypass their setUp and tearDown routines. The fix should ensure that test cleanup code is not executed for these skipped functions, thereby preventing unintended errors during debugging. The expected behavior is that for test functions decorated with a skip marker, neither setUp nor tearDown is run.
feature1.hint_texts: Focus on ensuring that for tests skipped at the function level (using decorators such as @unittest.skip or @pytest.mark.skip), the condition in the runtest method correctly checks the test object's skip status (_is_skipped(self.obj)). Developers should verify that when --pdb is active, no call to setUp or tearDown is made for these tests. Review the existing logic inherited from the previous fix and ensure it remains stable for function-level skipped tests.
feature1.entrypoint: File: src/_pytest/unittest.py – In the runtest() method, examine the if statement that checks for the usepdb option and _is_skipped(self.obj). This is the starting point for adjustments specific to individual (function-level) skipped tests.

feature2.prompt: Fix the issue where unittest.TestCase.tearDown is executed for entire test classes marked with @unittest.skip when running with --pdb. The fix should guarantee that for a test class decorated as skipped, neither setUp nor tearDown is invoked, thus preventing errors during debugging. The expected behavior is that a skipped test class does not trigger any test lifecycle methods that could lead to unintended side effects.
feature2.hint_texts: Extend the existing logic to also account for tests that are skipped at the class level. Developers should add a condition in the runtest() method to check the skip status of the parent test object (using _is_skipped(self.parent.obj)) and integrate it with the existing check. This will ensure that when --pdb is active, no test lifecycle methods are executed for an entire skipped class. Pay special attention to preventing errors such as NameError during teardown.
feature2.entrypoint: File: src/_pytest/unittest.py – In the runtest() method, update the condition by introducing a check for _is_skipped(self.parent.obj) alongside _is_skipped(self.obj). Also, refer to the modifications in testing/test_unittest.py where the test function test_pdb_teardown_skipped_for_classes is defined.

collaboration_points.shared_resources: Both features modify the runtest() method in src/_pytest/unittest.py and rely on the skip-checking utility (_is_skipped). Additionally, the tests defined in testing/test_unittest.py serve as shared validation for the overall behavior.
collaboration_points.integration_strategy: The two features must be integrated by ensuring that the unified skip logic in runtest() correctly combines the checks for both function-level (_is_skipped(self.obj)) and class-level (_is_skipped(self.parent.obj)) skip markers. Developers should review the combined condition to verify that no regressions occur in either scenario.
collaboration_points.communication_needs: Developers implementing each feature must coordinate on the refactoring of the runtest() method, particularly agreeing on the naming conventions (such as for any tracking variables) and the integration of the new class-level skip check. Regular communication is needed to ensure the unified behavior works seamlessly in --pdb mode.
